bounded_conclusions: The production +u_A/dt slope is the partial derivative of the affine q_u extension with qbot and u held fixed.
Along the frozen E4 B3 predictor family, dqbot/dH approximately cancels +u_A/dt; the frozen-u total derivative is approximately zero to O(1e-8) relative to the production partial slope.
Allowing the pointwise u_A value to vary leaves the total q_u derivative only O(1e-6) of the production partial slope over the preregistered plateau points.
Therefore production dq_u/dH=+u/dt must not be described as the total derivative of historical q_u across neighboring predictor states.

This distinction does not by itself imply the production iteration slope is invalid, because an iteration-response policy may intentionally be a partial affine extension rather than a physical total derivative.
links_to_prior_evidence: MAP03: in the simple corrector fixture, u locally matches physical storage sensitivity while bottom-outward exchange sensitivity is -u.
MAP04/MAP05A: nonzero iteration slope policies can converge to physically equivalent accepted states when their corrector path remains admissible.
MAP05: removing slope entirely can alter the path enough to hit a narrow corrector-domain failure in the stronger B3 case.
forbidden_inference: Do not relabel +u/dt as a physical interface-exchange Jacobian.
Do not call the partial-versus-total distinction a production defect without an explicit coupling-contract requirement.
Do not change production code from this retrospective calculation alone.
